extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians and researchers considering submitting to or reading the Israel Journal of Mathematics (authors, readers, and referees)
extracted.subtask_short: submitting to Israel Journal of Mathematics
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and high-level standards for research papers considered by the Israel Journal of Mathematics: scope, expected originality/quality, editorial contact about peer-review timing, and journal-level metrics/indexing information. Intended to help authors assess fit and practical expectations for submission/review.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-quality, original research papers
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Israel Journal of Mathematics publishes high-quality, original research papers across a broad range of pure and applied mathematics."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implied evaluative requirement: submissions should be original research and of high scholarly quality. The page presents originality and overall quality as primary acceptance criteria (no further submission rules or formatting details provided on this page).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope / Subject-area fit
rubrics_metrics.description: "Showcases a diversity of subjects, including set theory, model theory, algebra, group theory, number theory, mathematical analysis, ergodic theory, algebraic topology, geometry, combinatorics, mathematical physics, and applied and computational mathematics."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manuscripts should fall within these listed areas of pure and applied mathematics; fit to the journal's topical scope is an implicit criterion for consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer-review timeline flexibility (COVID-19)
rubrics_metrics.description: "As a result of the significant disruption that is being caused by the COVID-19 pandemic we are very aware that many researchers will have difficulty in meeting the timelines associated with our peer review process during normal times. Please do let us know if you need additional time. Our systems will continue to remind you of the original timelines but we intend to be highly flexible at this time."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational guidance for authors and reviewers: if extra time is needed for review or revision due to pandemic-related disruption, contact the journal; standard automated reminders may still be sent but the journal will consider extensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Journal-level performance metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Listed journal metrics (as indicators of journal standing): "Journal Impact Factor 0.8 (2024)", "5-year Journal Impact Factor 0.8 (2024)", "Downloads 139.5k (2025)".
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These figures are presented as contextual metrics about the journal (useful for authors assessing reach and impact), not as manuscript-evaluation criteria. Authors may use them to gauge visibility and influence of publishing here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indexing and discoverability
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal is "Abstracted and indexed in" numerous services (BFI List; Baidu; CLOCKSS; CNKI; CNPIEC; Chinese Academy of Medical Science (CAMS); Current Contents/Physical, Chemical and Earth Sciences; Dimensions; EBSCO; Google Scholar; INIS Atomindex; JST; Mathematical Reviews; Naver; OCLC WorldCat Discovery Service; Ovid Discovery; Portico; ProQuest; SCImago; SCOPUS; Science Citation Index Expanded (SCIE); TD Net Discovery Service; Wanfang; eLibrary.ru; zbMATH).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates broad indexing and discoverability of published articles—useful information for authors about where published work will be visible; not a submission-style rubric but relevant to authors' publication decisions.
